paragraphs.source_en: The appearance of pottery in the 10th millennium BP was almost contemporaneous over a large area including the northern Niger and the southern Algeria. The two more distant localities where the oldest ceramics were documented, namely the Tagalagal in the Air and Tin Hanakaten in the Tassili, were separated by more than 600 kilometres. The fact that both areas present a similar decoration on pottery produced at the same time, indicates that contacts between people in these two areas existed

paragraphs.source_en: A similar type of pottery which appeared simultaneously over a vast region testifies not only to an extremely quick diffusion of this new technique but also to a continuous network of communication and frequent contacts between inhabitants of the main Central Saharan massifs. Only few studies on the origin of clay sources for pottery manufacture are known but in most cases the production was local. In the case of the Adrar Bous site and the Acacus sites the pottery was made locally, whereas at Tagalagal pottery manufacturing took place elsewhere, with the supply areas from 25 and 75 km away (Roset 1996; Di Lernia 1999).

units.source_en: In the case of the Adrar Bous site and the Acacus sites the pottery was made locally, whereas at Tagalagal pottery manufacturing took place elsewhere, with the supply areas from 25 and 75 km away (Roset 1996; Di Lernia 1999).

paragraphs.source_en: The circulation of ideas and perhaps of people was not limited to the Central Saharan massifs. One of the most frequent motifs of pottery decoration, the so-called dotted wavy line, has a very wide spatio-temporal distribution. It is found in sites as far separated as the Khartoum area of the Nile Valley, Tagalagal in north Niger and at Tin Torha in Libya; and a similar type of pottery has also been found in East Africa, near Lake Turkana (Haaland 1992; Roset 1996). The fact that some decorative motifs on pottery remained unchanged for more than two thousand years indicates not only a great conservatism in this production but also its homogeneity among different and often very distant groups.
